From now on, we will expect that the accused avoids lengthy speeches and repetition and keeps his questions short. Likewise, we shall expect that the witness avoid personal argument and comments on and to the accused and answers the questions as shortly as possible. Mr. Milosevic, if you want to test the credibility of this witness, you should do so now. There is much of his evidence which has been left untested by your concentration and repetition of preliminary matter. As you know, your time will be limited, so we suggest that you move on to other topics. And if you want to cross-examine about the statement, you should do so as soon as possible. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I shall cross-examine in the order that I have made for myself. I have it down here, and it follows his own statement. As for time, I assume that you are duty-bound to give me more time than the Prosecutor had, in view of the written documents that he provided. So I shall continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I quoted to you awhile ago the last one of these documents, and it is obvious that half of the papers presented were about the independence of Kosovo. Is what I read correct, that the historian Dusan Matkovic which was the Ambassador of Yugoslavia in Greece today said, in March 1998, that he was, I quote, "surprised and appalled when Tanic, at the talks between the Serb and Albanians intellectuals in Munich in the organisation of the Bertelsmann Foundation concerning the problem of Kosovo, quite coolly discussed the possibility of Kosovo becoming an independent state." Just yes or no; is it correct?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This statement was denied, that is to say that it was given in the wrong context.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You denied it. Let's go on. In your statement, on page 9 - I'll go back to that - it's page 9 in the Serbian translation of the statement, you said that in Kosovo, on the 25th of June, I made a speech in which I annulled all the results of the negotiations which you had held until then. I looked at that speech. I have it. So I'm going to ask you the following: Why do you think that anything was said in a -- against the Albanians in that speech? I'm not talking about your results because I first heard of your results over here. So Politika, the daily newspaper, published all of this. In this area, there should be a policy of national equality of rights.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: This is precisely the point which I had in mind. How can the witness follow this? What is the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please. Where is there anything here which jeopardises the rights of Albanians? Because he claims that in my speech, I simply brought into question those rights of theirs. So where does it say that here? I'm quoting, and the newspapers are a kind of history. They cannot be rewritten for the same dates. So it's the 25th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No need to give us any comment about the newspapers. What is that -- you're asking about the speech, are you, of the 25th of June, 1997, referred to in the witness's statement; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What is you're putting about that speech?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I want him to answer the following question: Where in my speech was there any reference to anything that would jeopardise the rights of Albanians? So I'm quoting this to him. "In this area there should be a policy of national equality of rights, a spirit of tolerance should prevail. Everything that characterises a humane, democratic society." Now I'm going to skip a part, and then it says: "I believe that now is the time for the forces who wish their country and their people well, to unite in order to achieve the results that we wish to achieve in terms of reforms and development, and I hope that in this way this town and all of Kosovo and Metohija is going to give their contribution." Then furthermore: "As for the work of state organs, they should act in accordance with the law, notably in Kosovo, because the possibilities for discrimination are greater than in other parts of the republic, several times greater, at that. Our state has to be an example in terms of the state authority --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It's impossible for the witness to answer if you read out two or three minutes' worth of speech, as you've done. Just a moment. Mr. Tanic, you're being asked about the speech of the 25th of June, 1997, in Pristina, which the accused made, and he is claiming that there was nothing in it to jeopardise the rights of the Albanians. Now, can you help us about that? What is it that you say there was in the speech which had that effect?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As you know, I did not mention that speech in the statement and also when I testified. However, as far as I can remember, in order to be as precise as possible --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It's in your statement of the -- of 2000, and I have read what it says in it, and it's that you're being asked about. If it's wrong, just say it's wrong, but that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, no. It's not wrong. It's not inaccurate. It's just difficult for me to remember this precisely without having the speech itself. As far as I can remember, in that speech, Mr. Milosevic insisted on the following: That Kosovo be an integral part of Serbia and that he -- and that actually foreign mediation would not be accepted, as far as I can remember. I emphasise that. In that context, there is a certain impediment in the negotiations. I already said what was achieved in the negotiations, but there was foreign mediation already in the schooling negotiations. However, the return to autonomy meant broader autonomy within Serbia and Yugoslavia. So it would be a part of Serbia but not an integral part of Serbia. I would like to have a look at the speech in its entirety because people cannot simply take things out of context this way. I would have to refresh my own memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have quoted what can be checked out, but we can't waste time. I would just like to quote something else in order for it to be quite clear. This is a totally untruthful assertion that is being made here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We can get a copy of the speech, no doubt.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You will get it. It's Politika of the 26th of June.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters find it impossible to follow this debate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Will you listen to what the interpreters are saying. They are finding it impossible at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to speak really slowly now. So in addition to what I've quoted to you just now, in Prizren, I say particularly in this place and in this town, I want to tell you something that I consider to be the most important in this town, because in it, there are Serbs, Albanians, Muslims, Turks, Roma, and others. Every one of the ethnic groups, to a large proportion. That is why I believe that this town and this region should be an example of carrying out the policy of national equality of rights, a policy that would make it possible for all people to give -- to live on a footing of equality and under humane conditions, that there should be a high degree of mutual understanding and that a joint life of all citizens should be built successfully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Milosevic, which speech are you quoting from?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's from the same newspaper. I made a few speeches on that day in Pristina. I quoted a Pristina one at first and then in Prizren. That's the other one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So all of it is in Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let us stop there. Mr. Tanic, do you remember now whether the accused made a speech in Prizren that day, and what was in it? If you don't remember, just say so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not remember. I only referred to the speech in Pristina. But I would like to see it on the monitor, if possible, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. No, we're not going to go over it again. You can produce a copy of it in due course, Mr. Milosevic, as part of your case. The witness does not remember. So there's no point going on asking him about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Does he at least remember they were my generally-known public political positions, and I'm sure that equality, et cetera, et cetera, that this is the only key for life together in this town and in this region, and I am sure the only key to the success of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No need to go on reading it. You can ask the witness if he remembers that it was your - Mr. Milosevic's - publicly-known position that he believed in or he supported equality. Mr. Tanic, can you help us on that or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I remember that Mr. Milosevic supported this in declarative form but not in his political steps. I think there was a great deal of divergence between what he said and what he did, and that was the essence of the problem and the political debate.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let me move on since you're not going to allow me to Blank pages inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Pages 5085 to 5087. quote. This is a similar form of abuse as the 20 -- 89th of June [as interpreted] speech, which was also abused and misused. You said just now, Mr. Tanic, five minutes ago here and now, referring to the speech, that you do not know everything I said but that I insisted on the fact that Kosovo must be an integral part of Serbia, should be an integral part of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the reservation made that I might have some lapses in memory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. An integral part of Serbia. That was also a common position of mine and I consider that today, that today Kosovo is an integral part of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was not your view at the time at the negotiations. I apologise for interrupting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, as you challenge that and you represent the Novo Demokratija, are you aware of the fact that a document exists put out by the Novo Demokratija party which you can take from their website yourself - the date is the 19th of March, 1998 - in which, on page 1 of that document, point 2, it is -- the following is stated: As an integral part of the Republic of Serbia and, point 3, it says the relations between the autonomous province as an integral part of the Republic of Serbia, and then again, separate, individual, and collective rights of national minorities cannot be realised contrary to the constitution and legal provisions as well as internationally-recognised obligation of national minorities to express loyalty to the state within which -- of which they are part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let the witness -- let the witness see the document if you're going to put it to him. Show it to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will show it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let him see it, and then you can ask a question about it. Let him read it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot spend too much time, because you're going to subtract the time. I can give it to you and I can give it to the witness as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let the witness see it if you're going to ask him some questions about it. Mr. Tanic, if you would just look at that document. Don't say anything. Just read it briefly, and then it can be handed back to the accused.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can keep it. It's easy to get another copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now my question is as follows: His party --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let him finish reading it. Mr. Tanic, have you now had a chance of looking at that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What's your question, Mr. Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you said that I insisted upon the fact that Kosovo was an integral part of Serbia, and I don't deny that because I do consider it to be an integral part of Serbia - that is what I always considered; I consider now and shall consider in the future - and as you're making that comment from the standpoint of your party, is it clear from that document by your party that your party too considers Kosovo to be an integral part of Serbia and that therefore comments of your kind cannot have been presented from the standpoint of your party as representing your party? Is that correct or not?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not. May I quote a provision of the document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 5, it says: "Novo Demokratija considers that the broad autonomy of Kosovo and Metohija within the frameworks of the Republic of Serbia and Yugoslavia is the sole acceptable solution which respects the interests of Albanians from Kosovo and Metohija for the free expression of their own identity but the -- and the interests of Serbia for having full sovereignty on the territory." So broad competencies within the framework of Serbia and Yugoslavia. That was the formula and that was what Mr. Milosevic applied in the negotiations as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but you read out "and sovereignty on the whole of the territory." You've just quoted that, you've just read that out from that particular document, which also confirms the integral part of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Milosevic. This is a constitutional legal debate and we need to call an expert here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We're not having a debate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I'm going to interrupt this. I said there was to be no personal argument, and we meant it. Now, remember the interpreters too. Now, Mr. Milosevic, do you want us to have this document as an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It doesn't have any importance, but you can include it in any way you like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You claim that you hadn't met my wife, had meetings with my wife.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If the document can be brought back. Bring the document back. Give it back to Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I asked you, you claim that your met my wife. Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But not as your wife but as the leader of the JUL party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you answer me with a yes or no, it will save time.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is an unfortunate term, "wife."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what is the name of the political party of my wife?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is called the Yugoslav United Left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that that is not correct?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is how it was represented on the electoral list.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not as the Yugoslav United Left but as the Yugoslav Left. The name of the party is not the Yugoslav United Left. So you don't even know the name of the party that you say you cooperated with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You make that assertion, and it's pointless to go on. No doubt we can find out what the truth is. Now, let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was it founded?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I'm not an expert in matters of your party. We were coalition partners, I was not a member of JUL.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. So you don't know, then say so. Say "I don't know." Now, you claim you met me on the premises of the JUL party; right?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I meant the reception's head in JUL. It is the administrative building of the JUL party, which is where the receptions were held. It is used as a working premises and for official ceremonies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, we established that the receptions were in fact held in the garden, but let's move on. You claim in your written statement that you met me in the deputy's club secretly.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't say that. I didn't say secretly. I think that you were in the deputy's club on one occasion, but I threw out everything that I was not able to corroborate with independent sources. So that needn't be taken into account. I think we met each other once, but it wasn't in secret. It wasn't clandestinely, I think, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. As you're withdrawing that part of your statement, I'm not going to pursue the point. Now, you're claiming that while I was President of Serbia, you were in my cabinet, in my offices, and I'm going to quote. It is on page 3, and you say the following, the third paragraph from the top on page 3. You make mention there of the Presidency and the Federal Assembly building or, "in his personal cabinet to the left of entrance." Do you know that my cabinet, my office, is not to the left of the entrance? To the left of the entrance is the porter's premises, and then there's the kitchen, there's the large banquet hall, and my cabinet isn't there at all. The cabinet of the President of the Republic of Serbia is on the first floor, at the end of the corridor, and it is the one but last door. So it's not to the left of the entrance at all, which means that you were never there. Is that right or not?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not right, Mr. Milosevic. I was there at least twice. You keep sticking to this cabinet. You enter through the main entrance, you pass the radar control section, like you do at an airport. As far as I remember, you would go into the big hall on left where we have had meetings, and there are at least two different photographs from two different occasions. I thought that that was where your cabinet was as well, because on one occasion you left the meeting for a brief period of time and said you were going right next door to your cabinet. So those were the official ceremonial halls of the Presidency of Serbia and there are photographs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, it says here that you met me in my personal cabinet to the left of the entrance, and now you're saying --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I'm just wondering how you managed to sell all this.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a very great insult. I cannot allow that even on pain of seeming arrogant myself, that I sold anything to anyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, this Tribunal is not a nursery, a kindergarten for me to be able to sell something to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Stop this personal argument. Mr. Milosevic, if you want this to continue, you must stop, and that is an official warning, that if you go on in this way, then the cross-examination will be brought to a close. Mr. Tanic, too. I've told you before. Resist the temptation to personalise this. Now, if you've got a proper question, Mr. Milosevic, ask it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have many questions, Mr. May.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you make mention of my wife and the meetings you had with her, tell me, please, what function she held in JUL in the JUL party during the time you allege.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mrs. Markovic was the president of the administration or directorate of JUL, as far as Mr. Markovic told me, and it was a long working meeting with the foreign representatives linked to the topic of Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what month was this in 1994? As you said that I called upon the Novo Demokratija and you to the new coalition meeting?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'd have to refresh my memory on that score. Your proposal was sent to the operation, the Civil Alliance of Serbia, the Novo Demokratija. The Serb SPO and Civil Alliance had a different view from the Novo Demokratija party. I didn't say that you invited Novo Demokratija alone but that Novo Demokratija accepted your invitation that you sent out to the opposition to form a coalition government to strengthen the Dayton peace process. So please doesn't try to divert my words, if you would.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As in your statement, you use the term very frequently, "discreet negotiations." You seem to use that term. Could you please explain to me what you mean by "discreet negotiations"? What does the term "discreet negotiations" denote? What does it mean?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your express desire linked to the preparation for a political agreement to Kosovo was that all this should be done in a discreet manner so that if the outcome was not a positive one, that the three parties of the coalition party should not lose face and so that the Albanian secessionist movement should not gain the advantage, and that is why they were discreet. Sometimes people knew about them, sometimes they didn't. Some were very public, some were ultra-secret and confidential, sometimes semi-secret, and it all took three years. The process was a three-year-long process in which some ten other people took part in addition to myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you consider that what your party published denying all that is incorrect; right?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it -- I -- what -- my party's statement is not correct, and I said that we could be witnesses here to show that, demonstrate that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who invited you, allegedly, to attend that first meeting, which, as you claim, you had with me?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the president of the Novo Demokratija party, Mr. Mihajlovic, included me into the delegation which went to have a working meeting with you to ascertain the joint platform on several topics. This was done at least once a year and probably more often.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. So Dusan Mihajlovic invited you.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did not invite me, he made me a member of the delegation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Now in the period that you're testifying to, did you hold any state function whatsoever?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never performed any official state function nor did I say I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you. So just say no, and let's move on.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not state but party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that period of time - you're talking about 1994, 1995 - did you -- were you in any way known as a public figure? Were you recognised as a public figure?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, up until then, were you at the head of any information institution?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not up until then. Nor afterwards. I wasn't at the head of any information institution. For a brief period of time, I was president of the executive board of a monthly journal, but only for several months and I didn't deal with any informational media work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you enumerate the results of your work to stabilise relations with the leaders of the Kosovo Albanians.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My results thus far did not exist because I didn't work on that question, especially not from the positions of an opposition party. All we did was have a few friendly meetings, and a study was published, but until then, there were no discreet talks, political dialogues, negotiations or anything of that kind. So how can there be results on something that did not in fact exist as yet at the time?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many contacts did you have of that nature up until 1994? Personal contacts, the kind that you're mentioning now.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at least ten. We're talking about the period that is not incorporated into my statement at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Since, until then, your party did not participate in government, which state authority authorised you to participate in this process?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just said that I did not take part in any kind of negotiations. There weren't any negotiations. I'm sorry. Please do not push me into verbal traps yet again. In addition to that, I had just joined Novo Demokratija a short while before that. I did not take part in any negotiations in an unauthorised manner. There weren't any negotiations in 1994. Contacts are not negotiations. When they were, they were discreet negotiations and there was a political dialogue and you authorised them for the parties belonging to the ruling coalition and that is something that is a well-known fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You claim that you were the chief negotiator in the discreet negotiations with the Albanians; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Did I claim that during my testimony? As far as I know, I did not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He did not claim that. So you mustn't put things which he didn't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. All right. We'll get to that. Let me just have a look at something. I'll find that. I can't find it right now, but this does exist in the statement, in Mr. Tanic's statement, so we'll get to that later. Because you claimed that this role you got or deserved, first and foremost, because you had good relations with the representatives of the Kosovo Albanians; is that right or is that not right?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but personal contacts are one thing and negotiations are another thing. And please restrict yourself to what my testimony consisted of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Not only with them but also with representatives of the international community and also because, from a security point of view, you were acceptable to the SDB. Did I understand you correctly in response to my question?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I understood the people that I was in contact with, that is how you understood me. Having good personal contacts is not a forbidden thing; right?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I put my question very precisely. You say that you got this mission because of your good contacts and relations with the Kosovo Albanians, with the representatives of the international community, and also the SDB.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had good personal relations with the representatives of the Kosovo Albanians, good personal relations with the representatives of the international community, the service of the state security gave security guarantees for me before I saw you. This is a formal administrative matter, and please do not make me answer things I did not mention during my testimony and not even in my statement. The statement was given --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You will not -- you will not be required to answer unfair questions, Mr. Tanic, but would you do your best shortly to answer such questions as there are. The more quickly you answer the questions, the sooner this will finish. Mr. Milosevic, don't put things which he didn't say in his evidence, and we'll get on more quickly. Yes. Next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you say here, verbatim, that you were authorised for negotiations with the Albanians first of all from Dusan Mihajlovic, the head of your party, thirdly from the SDB -- thirdly from me, and secondly from the SDB? Is that what you said here?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I had authorisation from Mr. Dusan Mihajlovic and also authorisation from you and from the State Security Service. These are two different things, although they pertain to the same matter. I never introduced myself as some agent of the state security, Mr. Milosevic. Authorisation is one thing; guarantee is another thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I do not see any difference between full powers and authorisation except that one is a Serb word and the other is a word that is foreign, that is used in the Serb language. So really --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: This is all a matter of argument and a matter of comment. Now, what is the next question?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that also in 1999, you carried out the same activities on behalf of the SDB with interests defined by the SDB. Is that right or is that not right?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but I have to be reminded as to whether I said that during my testimony.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, yes, you did.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During my testimony?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was authorisation to seek a solution to bring the war with NATO to an end as soon as possible, but again we're talking about an authorisation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that everything --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, sorry to interrupt you. I want to go back to the answer given by the witness where he said he had authorisation from Mr. Dusan Mihajlovic and also authorisation from you. That's from you, Mr. Milosevic. I'd like to ask the witness: How did you get the authorisation from Mr. Milosevic? In what form?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Orally, during that first meeting that I mentioned, the meeting between our delegation and Mr. Milosevic in -- at the premises of the Presidency of Serbia. This was a working meeting and we presented our project of resolving the Kosovo problem to Mr. Milosevic in three stages that I already mentioned, three stages, first confidence building measures and then political engagement, Mr. Milosevic looked at that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... authorisation from him in the presence of others?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Mr. Mihajlovic was present and the other members of the delegation. Mr. Milosevic said explicitly, "That is all right, you can continue along those lines." This is clear authorisation. He did not put any objections to persons or --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So that was at a meeting with the delegation of Novo Demokratija. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is what it says on page 3, at the very beginning of your written statement. "As a member of Novo Demokratija --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let the witness have a copy of his statement. If he has one in front of him; if not, in the original if it is in the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, doesn't the witness know what he was saying? What does he need a copy of the statement for?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, the -- he's entitled to have a copy of a statement which you're going to ask him questions on which is no less than 41 pages long. He's perfectly entitled to have a copy of that. Now, it's -- it's page --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 3, at the very beginning, it says: "As a member of Novo Demokratija and special advisor to Dusan Mihajlovic, the president of ND --" that is to say Novo Demokratija -- "on international relations in Kosovo." So he was involved in international relations and Kosovo. "I was chosen to conduct these discreet negotiations with the Kosovo Albanians. I received this authorisation directly from Milosevic at a meeting that I and Dusan Mihajlovic held with him in approximately 1995."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First and foremost, I still haven't received a copy of the statement. I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He must have one in his own language.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you can confirm to him that I rightly quoted what I said in terms of his statement, because you have his statement in front of you. And let me proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Nice -- Mr. Nice, have we got a copy of this?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: We'll get one in his own language. He does actually speak and read English to a reasonably high level or a high level. Here it comes, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Tanic, you're being asked about the top of page 2 in the English, beginning: "As a member of the ND party and special advisor to Dusan Mihajlovic..." If you have that passage.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes. I've found it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. What's the question now, Mr. Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question pertains to the previous answer given by Mr. Tanic, that I authorised him at the meeting held with the delegation of Novo Demokratija that I had received. He described the composition of the delegation and where various issues were mentioned. And in the statement, he said that I authorised him at a meeting that he and Dusan Mihajlovic had with me. So when were you telling the truth; a short while ago or when you made this statement?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The question is very unfair. I said the truth on both occasions. I'm not duty-bound to mention all the participants in the meeting. After all, the statement was made in its working version and what is truly valid is what I said when giving evidence here. So it's really unfair. After all, I could not deal with this for three years had I not had this authorisation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... just make sure that the transcript contains my comment, which it doesn't. Mr. Tanic, if a question is unfair, we will stop it. Now, the witness, the accused, rather, is entitled to put to you things which are in your statement. What he's not entitled to do is to misrepresent what you said in evidence. Yes. What's the next question, Mr. Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A short while ago, you said that you had never stated that you were the chief negotiator.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And you, Mr. May, also said that the witness never stated that he was the chief negotiator.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's why I ask you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: In his evidence, he did not say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. That's why I'm asking you to look at line 1 of the next paragraph on the same page, where it says: "I was the principal negotiator in these discreet negotiations." Full stop. Is that what is written down here or not? "I was the principal negotiator in these discreet negotiations." Full stop, that's the whole sentence. Didn't the witness a minute ago say that he --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let the witness answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, the description while I was giving this written statement, which was of a working nature, is not the same thing as giving evidence in court. I gave a broader context so the Prosecution could understand the context involved. In that context, I was one of the driving forces of these negotiations because the president of my party and I advocated these negotiations with the Albanians the most and because I was the person who prepared the largest quantity of useful documents, and I dealt with this with two or three different sides and it is in that context that I used this. And secondly, if we are going to talk about the English language, principal negotiator, main negotiator, whatever, I already said that these were political negotiations. This is a working version. Everything that belongs to this working version and that is taken out of context is quite unfair, all such questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So, Mr. Tanic, what you're really saying is that what you were one of the driving forces in the negotiations, not the principal negotiator.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, from a formal and legal point of view, I was not a negotiator. That is not even in the written statement. It doesn't say in legal and formal terms. I was in the discreet negotiations.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you believe when I quote your statement verbatim, without any comment, where it says, "I was the principal negotiator in these discreet negotiations --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You've made the point. The witness has answered. Now, let's move on. You can comment to us in due course but not now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were with Dusan Mihajlovic in my office. Not with the delegation, with Dusan Mihajlovic.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I explained during my answer that there were some other people. Please, again this is unfair. Again words are being put in my mouth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a moment. Let me put to this witness. I read over your statement, Mr. Tanic. It may seem as if that there were only three of you - Mr. Milosevic, Mr. Mihajlovic, and you - and there you were given specifically for the negotiation, and now your version of the story is a little bit different. Why is that? Could you clarify that matter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will clarify that very gladly. The accused, Mr. Milosevic, is denying everything, starting from my very existence all the way up to my role. My position is that during my testimony before this Court, I'm going to say only things that can also be corroborated from two or three independent sources in addition. Mr. Mihajlovic did meet Mr. Milosevic many more times than I did, and he came to see me many times with very clear agreements, very clear authorisations. I do not want to talk about anything that cannot be confirmed from two or three independent additional sources. That is why my testimony in a formal sense is always more modest, whereas the written working version describes the broader context, but I'm not going to describe all of this during my testimony here, in order not to bring myself into a troublesome situation. I've had enough trouble as it's been.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a moment. Let me ask one more question about the authorisation. Was the authorisation at the time was specifically for the negotiations with Albanians or was that only for the -- in general terms for the three-phase policy of New Democracy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It related to the policy and to my participation. I can literally repeat Mr. Milosevic's words: "This is a good platform, continue that way." And later on, on several occasions, I had confirmation of this from Mr. Mihajlovic that at meetings where I was not present, that Mr. Milosevic and his associates agreed with this and that we can continue that way, and this was even mentioned in certain interviews, et cetera. I could not deal with this in public for three years without having had an authorisation. Somebody could have asked me what I was doing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So it is true that there wasn't any specific mention about the specific negotiations at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, no. I'm sorry. Mr. Milosevic was quite clear. He said that the three parties of the ruling coalition should go for negotiations. This question was not mentioned in Dayton, that we have some kind of an obligation to work this question out internally, that it would only be the parties from the ruling coalition that would deal with this, first that the negotiations should be prepared in a discreet way and then if a general negotiating platform is adopted, then the participants in the negotiations would withdraw and then, of course, Mr. Milosevic and Mr. Rugova would come into the picture as persons who would sign the agreement. And if -- if there is no previous agreement that is reached, then it would not get up to that level. And this is typical political technique. This is not something that is any kind of Serb speciality. We wanted this tinderbox to be defused before it exploded, so that was the formulation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Milosevic, continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before whom?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What's the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question is: Before whom? You say this was a formulation before everyone, as far as I understood it. Now, who is the "everyone" in the statement?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Dusan Mihajlovic was present, but so were the other members of the delegation. So where's the problem there? It was specifically stated in my statement that we were talking about a delegation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that's why I'm asking you. You say there was a delegation, but here it says that there was you and Dusan Mihajlovic and not a delegation. When were you telling the truth; then or now?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's unfair. Once again, it is a verbal trick to abuse the free interpretation of the working version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. If you -- if you cannot answer a question, say so. If it's unfair, you will be stopped. But you can be asked about your statement. It's a perfectly proper question. Yes. Mr. Milosevic, can we move on from this?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know precisely in connection with your testimony that Dusan Mihajlovic, last night, live on television, said that you, Mr. Tanic, could have only been an observer, like any other citizen of Serbia? And then he goes on to specify, "Well, at least if not like any other citizen of Serbia, then at least like those citizens of Serbia who are interested in political matters and nothing more than that." Do you know about that statement that he made last night that we were able to hear live via Television Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes I do. I know about it. But then I could have seen this as an observer, what I'm saying now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not as an observer of the event but "as an observer like any other citizen of Serbia who was interested in politics." That's what he said last night.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This statement by Mr. Mihajlovic does not correspond to the actual state of affairs at the time that these events took place, and this can be demonstrated and proved, but I don't think that that is the topic of --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you claim that he said an untruth yesterday; is that it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No need to comment. He's answered the question. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as I can see that you saw the statement, watched it, did you hear him support the stand and position taken by Mr. May or, rather, his question addressed to Mr. Nice, that is to say whether testimony of this kind can be taken into account at all?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. That's not a matter for the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the witness said that he watched it, watched the statement. So I'm asking you -- him whether he heard that being said as well. All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just -- wait a moment. Make sure this goes down on the transcript, which doesn't always follow. What I said was it doesn't matter. Yes. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. While we're on this third page, yesterday in the less than 40 minutes that I had left, I cleared up these questions with you, that is to say how many times you actually met me, and then we arrived at the conclusion, with Mr. May's help, that this was between five and seven times, at receptions and the like. Receptions of delegations of Novo Demokratija in JUL. So we said that this was five to seven times. We took note of that. How, then, can you explain, bearing this in mind as a pure fact that was established yesterday, how, then, do you explain what it says at the beginning here of -- in the last paragraph on that same third page, to save time, some -- "I met him some 20 times on public occasions such as state receptions," et cetera. How do you explain that, then, when we observed yesterday and the day before that it was five to seven times and here you say some 20, approximately 20 times? That's what you say in your statement. That is the beginning of the last paragraph on page 3.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, you said you'd never seen me in my life, so thank you for recognising that you saw me at least five to seven times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Don't argue. The question -- the question is for the witness. Mr. Tanic, in your statement, it says: "I met with him --" referring to the accused -- "approximately 20 times on public occasions such as state receptions." Now, then, can you assist the Trial Chamber as to how that appears in the statement, whether that's accurate or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct, and I -- my testimony was based on what can be proved by individual witnesses, otherwise, the statement is correct referring to a larger number of times on different occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please. Did we not establish yesterday that you claim that you saw me five to seven times?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You have asked the question. The discrepancy has been put, and he's given his explanation. So there's no point putting the same question again.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. There's no point asking questions in which the witness himself brings himself into a contradiction. That is quite clear to me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please. This is not fair. This is not fair. I have not brought myself into any kind of contradiction.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say here, you state here in your oral statement, in your testimony with respect to your cooperation with the State Security Service, that everything that you did had to have an authorisation from me. Is that what you said? Had to have my authorisation.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and that is true for anybody dealing in sensitive issues, in the field of state and national interests of Serbia and Yugoslavia. It didn't apply to me separately, it is a working principle. Please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And how come when you said later on that the service placed me under the -- under control, tapped my conversations, intercepted them and so on, do you consider that it had my authorisation to do so for what you say that the service did? Did it have my authorisation?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the winter of 1996, you attempted to cause civic unrest in Belgrade. From that time on, a certain number of people from the army, from the State Security Service monitored what you did, followed what you did because you wanted to create a civil war during the winter, during the demonstrations when you withdrew the police units and tried to provoke a clash between armed groups of demonstrators and the authorities and the opposition. From that time on, there was a certain - how shall I put it? - certain slight control. So you accused the top echelons of the security service and that a coup d'Etat was being prepared and that they were following your moves. So why do you make a problem for having accused him of doing so? They prevented the civil war that you wished to cause in Serbia in the winter of 1996. The army, the security service, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That's enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you've already broached that subject, how come people were armed on two sides without any incident breaking out? Nobody was killed, nobody was injured. How did -- how was that managed?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the demonstrators were killed -- was killed and then the army and the police, contrary to your instructions, set up a buffer zone and a corridor once again and that there are at least two public testimonies to that, but I know this from earlier on without these public testimonies. Without your knowledge, they set up a corridor again to prevent bloodshed. I think one demonstrator was certainly killed in Cikajubila Street [phoen] and perhaps another as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tanic, that was the day when I held my speech on Trazija Square, isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the day you organised a counter-rally of your people loyal to you to create clashes in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, how come, then, there weren't any?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the top echelons of the army and the police and the security services prevented you from doing so with the reformist politicians and afterwards suffered the consequences of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tanic, do you recall -- and this was seen by at least 300.000 people who were at that rally where I made my speech -- do you remember that throughout that mass of people from my office to the Moscow Hotel where there was a stage erected, I passed through those masses of people on foot? I walked there.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were your -- people loyal to you and your supporters. That's why you were able to pass through this mass on foot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I had several hundred thousand armed supporters, and wanted to create and cause a civil war, and I made this speech, which I think was a very nice speech, and then the masses dispersed. How can you construe things in that way?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You had about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: This is of no assistance to the Trial Chamber. You're well away from the evidence. I know the witness introduced it. We have gone on long enough about it. Now, let's move on to another topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you had the authorisation of the State Security Service as well, and here on page 3, in the second sentence of paragraph 2, right after the one in which you say that you were the principal negotiator, you say: "From my contacts with the SDB --" that is the state security service -- "and especially with Mijatovic and Stanisic --" so the chief of the State Security Service -- "I knew that the SDB did not systematically support anybody's efforts to negotiate with the Kosovo Albanians." Now, explain this to me, and my question is as follows: How come if the chief of the State Security Service, Mr. Stanisic, and the head of the Belgrade - you say he was chief of the Belgrade part of the security services; Stanisic was chief of the SDB of Serbia - now, if they told you and you understood that the SDB did not systematically support anybody's efforts to negotiate, how, then, could they authorise you to conduct those negotiations?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is quite obviously a typing error, because the statement was given in English and, yes, the sentence is nonsensical as it stands. As far as the names are concerned, Mr. Mijatovic and the other name, I said loud and clear yesterday during my testimony -- that is to say I mentioned these names. All the other discrepancies refer to what I said and can be supported and others that cannot be supported. But the translation is obviously incorrect because the sentence has no meaning. It is nonsensical. The sense of the sentence is that there are no other solutions, no other negotiating efforts were supported except those in which you were and Monsignor Paglia and myself and the president of my party, and Dojcilo Maslovaric, Ratko Markovic and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Never mind. We'll come to Paglia later on. So you're saying that these are typing errors, are they, what I'm asking you about? Typing errors in your statement; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That's what he said.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Very well. Very good.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tanic, I'm not clear as to exactly what you say the sentence should read. What are you saying the sentence should in fact read to make it correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I read it out, it is not clear to me either. The exact version is as follows: That the State Security Service did not systematically support any other negotiating effort except the one that I was included in, I was involved in. That's what I know. Otherwise, this is no secret. Our State Security Service was included in all the negotiations because of the exceptionally sensitive national situation and state situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I understand what you're saying it should read now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You've now said that in 1996, December, there was this rally after which you said that I was being watched and monitored. The date is December 1996. We can check that date out. How, then, could you answer yesterday to a question from Mr. Nice when he asked you whether your work throughout this time was known to me? And you said -- your answer was, "Absolutely so, via the service, because the service had to inform me." Why did it have to inform me? If I was under its supervision, as you claim, according to you, from the end of 1996, why did it have to inform me then?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Do you understand the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, I have understood the question, and I'll try and make my answer as concise as possible. First of all, I didn't say that you were under constant observation and surveillance but that you were subject to control from time to time. As far as incompatibility is concerned and to control your conduct and inform you regularly, there was nothing incompatible about that. You promised peace and as long as you strove for peace, everybody supported you. And why should you not be informed as to what was going on? It wasn't classical surveillance. It was a type of stepped-up control and supervision to see what you were doing, whether you wanted to bring about a new war, whether you were going to abide by the Dayton peace. This is no shame, this is something testified to by people from the army and politics and the state security services. In the papers, albeit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ah. So you're referring to the papers, are you?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not referring to the papers, I'm just saying that I'm not the first one to have said that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Judge Kwon has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt you, but before we go further. Mr. Tanic, when you answered the question regarding to the typing error just before, I noticed that you mentioned it as the statement was given in English. Is it true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it was. I speak English, but it's not my mother tongue. So sometimes some of the finer points escape me. And of course, there are translators who translate it. So I didn't make a single written statement in my mother tongue, actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said in your statement that with the English -- that you cooperated with the English service from the preparations of Dayton in 1993 onwards; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that there was a certain amount of working contact. Cooperation and working contact, those are two different concepts, particularly in this kind of work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But from 1993, is that right, that's what you said?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said 1993, 1994, for the simple reason that my memory might have lapsed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. We can set the transcript back. If I'm quoting you, we don't have establish what you said. You said you cooperated with them from preparations for Dayton in 1993 onwards. Did you say that or did you not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Or we can ask the Registrar to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, he said that. From preparations for Dayton.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now do you know that in 1993, not even the Americans knew about Dayton?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. This is quite an unfair question. When I said that it was preparations for Dayton, I meant preparations for peace agreement. They didn't know, of course, that it would be held in Dayton. It could have been held in any other town. A peace agreement in Bosnia was being prepared since 1993 and Dayton was decided as the locality much later on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not talking about Dayton in the geographic sense either but in the sense of a peace agreement, and do you know that in 1993, which is the year you quote for Dayton preparations, the Vance-Owen Plan was topical in fact and no Dayton at all? It was Vance-Owen, the Vance-Owen Plan.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the Vance-Owen Plan was topical, but it was an idea to hold a mass conference which would definitely put paid to all questions of Yugoslavia's disintegration and war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please. The Vance-Owen Plan was an integral plan, a comprehensive plan and did not imply any further conference. It was signed in Athens in 1993, and was not accepted later on, that doesn't matter, that's not essential, let's not now go into that matter, but the Vance-Owen Plan was in 1993. And do you know that one year later, we had the European Union plan which the Serbs also accepted but was not accepted by the Muslims, and that fell through too? Do you therefore know that as regards these preparations which you call preparations for Dayton, there could have been no mention of that either in 1993 or in 1994?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First and foremost, I'm here --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We'll wait and pause between question and answer. What is the point of this question, Mr. Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the point of the question, like of all other questions, because this is a completely false witness, is that he cooperated with the intelligence service of Great Britain in preparing Dayton from 1993 onwards. That's his claim. And in 1993, we had the Vance-Owen Plan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, we know. You have repeated that several times. Now, what is the question for the witness? Is the question supposed to be this: He could not have been -- he could not have been cooperating for a peace agreement because there were no preparations at the time. Is that the point?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is the point, but the question reads as follows --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let the witness answer your point.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First and foremost, Great Britain was always interested in all peace solutions and always supported them, including Bosnia. Secondly, I'm not here to testify about Bosnia, I'm here to testify about Kosovo. Thirdly, I was not 100 per cent precise when I was talking about background. We're talking about the end of 1993, the beginning of 1994. I'm aware of the fact that I said 1993 but I'm referring to the end of 1993. There were peace preparations even before the period, before -- that Milosevic is referring to. And as for Dayton, there were preparations much earlier than what he has been saying and, if you really want to, I can give you some further details.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I go on with my questions?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not a witness for Bosnia and Dayton, this is just a background explanation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I mentioned Dayton because Mr. Tanic mentioned Dayton.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. It's time -- it's time for the adjournment. We will adjourn now for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since in 1993, when you say that you cooperated with the British intelligence service, and from then onwards, there was no mention of Dayton or peace agreements, what was your cooperation all about then? What did it pertain to?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have explained that this was a question of working contacts, not cooperation. Could I please note here cooperation once again because I spelled this out very precisely. And these were preparations for a peace agreement generally speaking. Of course, the town of Dayton was not mentioned at that stage yet. There were other issues brought up as well, but it was obvious that a broad international conference was needed that would simply be of a stronger nature than various particular agreements. However, I repeat, I'm not here to testify about Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, then, as for this cooperation with the British intelligence service, did you have authorisation from Dusan Mihajlovic about that as well?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. And that was not cooperation. This was just contact and nothing else stemmed from that. No other activities stemmed from that. No other joint activities or anything. It was just an exchange of views. This was no act of cooperation, and I never used the word "cooperation." Please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I wrote down what you said, and it's also recorded on a tape in Belgrade and here, that you cooperated on the preparations of Dayton from 1993 onwards.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, end of 1993, beginning of 1994. I apologise to the Trial Chamber and to you. I'm sorry if I made a mistake. We're talking about a great many years. I can make a mistake. I gave a statement in English, and then after that, I testified only about things that I can prove from independent sources as well. And now you are trying to catch me in making minor errors rather than dwelling on the main points.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These are only main points.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first of all, I've proven that I've seen you and you claim that you've never seen me in your life.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I did not say that we had seen me [as interpreted]. I said that yesterday you said that we met five or seven times and in the statement you wrote 20 times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We have been over that point. We're not returning to it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Since Milosevic [as interpreted] did not authorise you to cooperate with the British intelligence service, he therefore authorised you only to carry out discreet negotiations with Albanians; is that your claim?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not cooperate with the British intelligence service and I'm not going to answer a question that is unfair. Mr. Milosevic keeps repeating a formulation that is evocative of espionage and I know that that's the point he's trying to make.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We will look at what was said. My note of the evidence given was that he had working contacts with intelligence services - the United Kingdom, Italy and Russia - in cooperation on analytical affairs. This work was known to all, including the accused. Does that represent the position, Mr. Tanic, or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, except that I spelled this out precisely, that this refers to the intelligence aspect of legal political issues such as peace agreements and the struggle against terrorism and negotiations with warring parties, an analysis of the victims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Now, Mr. Milosevic, have you got a new point? Let's go on to that. On this topic by all means, but let us have a new point rather than arguing what the witness said before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, since Mihajlovic did not authorise you for this cooperation, who authorised you for this cooperation with intelligence services?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not cooperation, it was working contacts. Please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Who authorised you for that which you claim were working contacts?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not what I claim, that is the way it was. These were working contacts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Who authorised you for what you say were working contacts?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For that which were working contacts, there was authorisation from the State Security Service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Then I can conclude that on behalf of the State Security Service of Serbia, you had working contacts with the British intelligence service from 1993.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You cannot conclude that at all, Mr. Milosevic, not even with the assistance of science fiction. Please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is just what you said just awhile ago.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, way. I never said that, neither in my statement or in my testimony, not five minutes ago, not five hours ago. This is malicious construction on your part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What are you complaining of, Mr. Tanic? Is it that you say the misrepresentation is that it was on behalf of the State Security Service? Is that the point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Well, it's been misrepresented. When you say "on behalf of," that infers other things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. We have the point. Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You say the State Security Service authorised you for something in relation to these working contacts. What for?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The service authorised this to the extent to which this assisted understanding between the two countries and also peace and integration processes in the territory of the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at whose initiative was it you that was chosen for this? At the initiative at the State Security Service or at the initiative of the British intelligence service?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The question is unfair, and it goes beyond the context of my testimony, to the best of my understanding.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's not for you to say.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said to the best of my understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The question is: Who chose you to do this work, if anybody chose you, or at whose initiative did you work this work?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The initiative came from both sides. It was mutual. As for political issues, they -- there is always initiative on both sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It had to do with your very own personality, coming from both sides; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's quite obvious. It pertained to the questions I mentioned, legal political questions, and it was mutual. It was not an initiative, it was a mutual approval.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean from a personal point of view, there was mutual consent that it should be you; right?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That it can be me too, Mr. Milosevic, because there were other people involved as well, probably persons who were closer associates of yours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who were these other people who cooperated with the British service?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not say cooperated with the British service. There were other people. There were other people as well. Who, with the knowledge of our state authorities, had contacts with foreign intelligence services in relation to legal political issues. I already said that the director of the CIA came to Belgrade on an official visit. This is no secret. Please. It is not a drama. These are legal political questions. I'm not talking about espionage. Nobody dealt in espionage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My only question was who were these other people? Just as you have this name Stanic, there are other people as well. What are their names?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My name is Tanic, please do not mispronounce it. And your head of state security had these contacts certainly with your knowledge. So it can be taken as you had had them too, Mr. Milosevic. He certainly did not secretly meet with the head of the CIA and then the newspapers found out. That is just one thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's go on. So Mihajlovic did not authorise you for that. He only authorised you for discreet negotiations with the Albanians; is that right? Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. Finally there's one thing we can agree upon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
