utterances.text: All right. In which capacity was it that he authorised you? As a member of the leadership or his special advisor or an official of Novo Demokratija or --

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As President of Novo Demokratija, he authorised me in my capacity as advisor to the President of Novo Demokratija and a member of the executive committee of Novo Demokratija at the very beginning and also a member of the presidential office of Novo Demokratija.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Could you please put this on the overhead projector. This is a record from Novo Demokratija or, rather, this is the admission paper of Mr. Tanic. This is a form of Novo Demokratija. At the beginning it says "Status," and there are three possibilities, A, founder, B, member, and C, sympathiser. It is the C that has a circle round it, that he's a sympathiser. He's not a member or a founder. Secondly, he signed this paper on the 18th of March, 1995, and this is his admission paper when he was admitted to Novo Demokratija. Please put this on the ELMO since Mr. Tanic said that he was a member of the leadership of the executive committee, a special advisor, that he was authorised by Mihajlovic. Please put this on the ELMO. Show it first to Mr. Tanic. Is that his admission paper?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let the witness see it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a photocopy of my admission paper. The signature corresponds to mine, but the status not. I'm going to ask the Court to request official papers from Novo Demokratija showing who members of the presidential office were and I kindly ask the Trial Chamber not to accept this document, even if Mr. Milosevic insists, if additional insight is not obtained into the records. So that means papers related to appointment, to appointments, to appointments to the presidential office and also a specific document that pertains to me. Please. I never misrepresented myself, and this is a great insult.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is there also a question related to education here? Does it say here that you are a university graduate? Did you deceive your colleagues at Novo Demokratija as well that you had a university degree? This is what it says here. Education, it says university degree.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did say that I studied at two different schools at the university. There is no contest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, to the best of my understanding, you never got a degree from any university. Education implies the degree you get. What school you finish, not schools that you attended to.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could not understand anything because I did not answer that question. I refused to answer that question because it's a private question, and I am not an expert witness here so that I would have to prove the level of my university education.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. So I'm asking Mr. May, Mr. Robinson, and Mr. Kwon now whether the witness should answer his question related to his education.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He has declined to do so. It's a matter which goes to his credibility. It's a matter which the Trial Chamber will weigh when considering the credibility of his evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let us hear what is on this document apart from education; in particular, the question of status.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The status is "sympathiser."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can say something straight away, and that is that either this is a forgery or a misunderstanding. And let me explain why. Because in addition to that, it says the number -- the record number is 39. Now, I don't think that the number of a party sympathisers is 39. They're usually hundreds of thousands. And the registration number indicates the narrow body of people that make up the leadership. Our executive board had 45 or 50 members and this is 39.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me remind you that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We're going to ask the document to be put on the ELMO and for the interpreters to try and interpret it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should like to draw your attention to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, I'm very interested in hearing the details, the data on this document, and if the interpreters can translate it, we'd be very grateful. The answers given to each query. Are the interpreters in a position to do that for us?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps somebody could read the actual words out for us.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I read them out?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the upper left-hand corner it says, "Status." Then A is "Osnivac," [phoen] meaning founder, B is member, and C - or V in the Cyrillic - is sympathiser. And it is the third, the word sympathiser that has been circled, which means the third variation, the third option. In the upper right-hand corner, it says Palilola [phoen], which is the municipality. So the number of this application form for admission refers to one particular municipality. And there are 187 municipalities in Serbia. Therefore, it is not the 39th member of the Novo Demokratija party but it is the 39th who joined as a sympathiser in the Palilola municipality.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not say I was the 39th member at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just a moment. We are dealing with the document and nothing else. Just read the document, if you would.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next we have the following titles: It says Movement, Recommendation, Name and Surname. That has been filled in and it says Ratomir Tanic. The address, it seems to be Kakovska Street [phoen], Belgrade, although it's a little bit illegible. The telephone not important. The personal identification number hasn't been entered. The date and place of birth --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could we have it moved up a bit, please? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says Marital Status, not filled in. Education, it says university. Profession is empty, Job or Profession, empty; Telephone/fax, empty; Hobbies, empty; Interests in the movement, empty; Region in which you would like to work, empty; Changes, empty. The date is the 18th of March, 1995 and a signature in his own hand in the bottom right-hand corner. That's all it says on this document. Let me just add to this from the papers, the denial published by Novo Demokratija where it says, "Ratomir Tanic is not a member but a sympathiser of the Novo Demokratija party, but as --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We're going to stop comment. We're going to stop comment. We're dealing with examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. The document will be exhibited. Defence Exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I provide some different kind of evidence and legal evidential material on what everything Mr. Milosevic -- everything that Mr. Milosevic has is his own private correspondence and I'm not interested in it. It means he received it from the Novo Demokratija party.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You can deal with that document. If you want to say something about it, you can.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I continue with my questions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. If he wants to say something about the document, he can. It's been put to him, and if he wants to give some sort of explanation, he can.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All I wish to say is that the document does not correspond to my actual status in the Novo Demokratija, and I suggest that, through legal channels, the Tribunal be provided with information as to my real status within the Novo Demokratija party plus some ten -- tens of interviews that were given as advisor to the President of Novo Demokratija over a three-year period. So I couldn't be just a sympathiser. But legitimate legal documents of Novo Demokratija, and I don't know why Mr. Milosevic is involving my former party in all this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It doesn't matter what you feel. Can we have an exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Defence Exhibit D10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were performing what you define, and I hope that I won't be wrong when I say political and intelligence research for these services that we mentioned, you received some form of assistance, material assistance; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. May I have the interpretation, please? I'm not getting it. My answer is no, that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you perform political and intelligence research? Is that true?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but at my own expense. And I did scientific research for my own party but at my own expense up until 1999, that is to say until the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And can you tell me what kind of professional qualifications you have for you to be able to engage in research work?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, "research work" has been defined here in the general sense, but the quality of research work is determined by the work itself, not whether somebody has some qualifications or not. I didn't wish to speak about that anyway and it's not work for the faculty. I wasn't a university professor for me to have, to have this. Research is a general concept, and you too use it in your terminology. You have to research into this problem and that problem and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, difficult, but you weren't able to know that because we never saw each other.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May it be entered into the LiveNote that the accused --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We are not going to have this interruption one of the other. You will ask questions and answers and leave a pause between them. There will not be interruption if this examination is to continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. May I continue now?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, you were asked by Mr. Nice at what level and how frequently you had meetings in the State Security Service, and in response to that question, your answer was two to three times a week. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said sometimes two or three times a week, sometimes once in two weeks, and depending on circumstances, this would vary. You can check it out. I didn't say that it was always two to three times a week. Sometimes in times of crisis, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So two or three times a week, contacts. You had, therefore, contacts more frequently than the Minister for the Interior with the State Security Service, it would appear.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Minister of the Interior, by virtue of his office, has daily contacts, and I mentioned just in times of crisis when these contacts would be stepped up. People try to do something useful, Mr. Milosevic, quite simply.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, as far as level is concerned, we've cleared up this two or three times a week as far as frequency is concerned, the frequency of the contacts. Now let's look at the level of those contacts. Your answer was leadership level; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have not cleared up the frequency issue, two or three times a week, because Mr. Milosevic has implied that I said all the time two or three times a week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. Let us not argue about that. Let's go on to the next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the next question was the following: First, at what level? Was I right in understanding that you said the leadership level of the State Security Service?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. You understood that quite correctly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let me just find this in your statement. Yes. All right. You therefore stated that, in connection with the creation of a coalition of the government of national unity, you talked about these questions, Kosovo issues, twice with Mihajlovic and five or six times with the SDB, the State Security Service. So the coalition had something to do with solutions to the Kosovo question. That's what you say.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you give me the page, please? I'm not able to follow.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm referring to what you said in your oral testimony.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When did I say this orally?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said this orally in your testimony. You said that one of the subjects of the formation of a coalition was the Kosovo question and that you discussed this twice with Mihajlovic and five or six times with the SDB, the State Security Service. You said that in your oral testimony.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do apologise, but --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you have it in the LiveNote, on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I'm going to stop this because of the argument that's going on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. We're not going to continue on this topic. You'll have to move on to another one. Mr. Milosevic, repetition, you've been criticised before. Don't repeat. Mr. Tanic, would you remember not to argue with the accused. You're giving evidence and not in some private argument with him. Would you therefore always leave a period after the question to allow interpretation to take place. Yes, Mr. Milosevic, go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said yesterday, in connection with a question from the Prosecutor as to the formula on the South Tyrol model, that you were not an advocate of that South Tyrol idea but it was Ratko Markovic.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that that platform was elaborated by Mr. Predrag Simic from the Institute for International Politics and Economics. He was the director. And that Mr. Ratko Markovic also supported it in a sense. I said that I wasn't very thrilled with that platform because it was far too costly and Belgrade didn't have that much money. The autonomy of South Tyrol is a very costly idea. This is an additional explanation that I'm making here today.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. How, then, in respect of your explanation, can we interpret your statement on page 5, paragraph 2, if you count the one from the previous page, and in that paragraph you say: "Second, my ideas were adopted by individuals close to Milosevic." Full stop. "For example, Ratko Markovic, Deputy Prime Minister of the Republic of Serbia, began, based on my suggestions, discussing a South Tyrol model for autonomy in Kosovo."

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You asked me or, rather, Mr. Nice, the Prosecutor, asked me what my opinion was of South Tyrol, and I said that I wasn't too thrilled with the idea. And even publicly, I advocated that kind of autonomy on several occasions, like I said in the statement, for the simple reason that at that time, it was the most acceptable type of model and platform where we could see eye-to-eye with the Albanian side. And let me give a more detailed explanation. The autonomy of South Tyrol is the ultimate status, refers to the ultimate status of Kosovo. And at the time, we had to find the least common, lowest common denominator for us to be able to start negotiations with the Albanians. So it is one thing what I privately thought myself and another thing what I had to do for political -- out of political necessity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you now say that, despite your private opinion, you made suggestions because you say, "On the basis of my suggestions, Ratko Markovic started discussing a South Tyrol model for autonomy in Kosovo." So he did that based on your suggestions which were contrary to your own convictions. That was when he started beginning to talk about the South Tyrol model.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, personal and political convictions differ. I entered into dialogue with the Albanians, although I wasn't too thrilled about them. So sometimes you have to do this for political interests. You have to do something that you're not very sure of privately speaking, but you say, "Well, let's go ahead with the dialogue," and you start one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The second stage, you say, is the reintegration of Kosovo Albanians into the political life of Serbia and Yugoslavia; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And who took part, in addition to Deputy Prime Minister Ratko Markovic, in those talks together with you?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that this was a political process which lasted three years, perhaps even longer. And in that process, Mr. Dojcilo Maslovaric took part, Mr. Ratko Markovic, Mr. Ratomir Vico, Mr. Percevic, Mr. Dusan Mihajlovic, myself, and a number of intellectuals who were linked to these three parties. And in the broadest possible scope, of course, free thinking intellectuals as well. There were probably some other people who took part, because, quite simply, it was a group activity which lasted over a long period of time. It was not just one negotiation, it was preparations for negotiations that went on for at least three years or, rather, two and a half to three years, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned Dojcilo Maslovaric as representative in the Vatican, the Holy See; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was later appointed the Yugoslav ambassador to the Vatican. Otherwise, he was a member of JUL, and he was there at the negotiations authorised by JUL. At least, that's what he said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you cooperate with Maslovaric most; in Belgrade, in Rome, or in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never said that we cooperated. I said that this was a group of people that did one and the same job. Even in the statement that was given in the English language and under much freer circumstances, I never represented this as a group of people that always sat together. They were the most different type of contacts but simply this was the group that work on these matters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And tell me now, in relation to which questions was it that my wife and Professor Ratko Markovic cooperated? Because that was your claim.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you please be so kind as to tell me which page or where I should look for this? Are you referring to the statement or are you referring to my testimony?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, for example, page 3, paragraph 2, towards the end, when you talk about Markovic and Maslovaric and you, that you were all working together, you say - that is the third line from the bottom of that paragraph - it says, "Both --" you're referring to Maslovaric and Markovic - "are closer to Milosevic and his wife Mira Markovic than I am." So I'm asking you, what did they cooperate on? On which matters did my wife and Ratko Markovic cooperate?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, you can see that, quite sincerely, I do not represent myself to be your associate, and I'm very glad that you mentioned that and that it says so in my statement, not only during my testimony. And I think that the two of them were close either to you or to her. I did not specify that Dojcilo Maslovaric was close to your wife as president of the directorate of the JUL party, and Ratko Markovic was closer to you, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you attend any one of their meetings? I mean meetings between my wife and one of them.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I attended meetings related to -- or, rather, a meeting between your wife and international representatives of Kosovo. Not your wife. Ratko Markovic and Dojcilo Maslovaric. I attended some meetings together with Mr. Ratko Markovic, but I did not interfere in any way in meetings between Ratko Markovic and your wife nor did I ever say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now you're claiming that my wife had meetings with Ratko Markovic, or did I misunderstand you?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You misunderstood me. I said that these two men were closer to you and your wife than I was. So I said this quite fairly, that I was not the main person around, as you keep telling me that I have been saying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am not putting that to you, that I made it up. It says here. This is what you wrote down in your own statement. "I was the principal negotiator." That's what you said. That's what you wrote down here. How can you say that it was me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We have now been over that. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just had to deal with that, what he said. This is quite unequivocal. He put it quite unequivocally, so I'm not the one who's saying it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many times did you come to the JUL premises anyway?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At least a few times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How come you don't know, then, that on the first floor in the street Djura Djakovica, there is not any kind of salon or a parlor, there's only an office?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, but where is there -- where is any reference made to the first floor? And usually these rooms, these conference rooms are downstairs, especially because this is a typical villa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's what it says, but let's not look for it now. This is a statement you made. It's in the transcript. So if you say that you did not make it, that's that.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, a conference room cannot be upstairs, but there are a few steps from the entrance. It's only four or five steps. I mean, it's not upstairs really.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. In order to enter the ground floor from the garden, you say that there are four or five steps; right?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The last time I was there was a number of years ago. And of course if I have to describe the villa, it's easier for me to draw it, with the permission of the Trial Chamber, that is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But then you would have to know that, from the garden, you have to climb up some steep steps in order to enter the ground floor.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But, Mr. Milosevic, it's not as high as an additional floor is. Perhaps just an extra landing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, yes, yes, but let's not go into all of that. Don't you tell me about it. When you say that I often had meetings at the JUL premises, tell me the name of at least one person that I received there.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that you often used receptions hosted by JUL for having meetings of your own during these receptions, and often you would have dinner after these receptions in a special room. If a working dinner is not an opportunity to meet your associates, I don't know what is but this is the narrowest circle of your associates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is untrue as well. But do you know that at such dinners there are at least about 30 people present, sometimes even more than that? And also that these dinners are hosted by the host, not me? That is to say, people coming from different structures.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, let's not deal with luncheons, dinners, stairs, steps, whatever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're the one who started it, not me.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but you're the one who asked me about the steps and stairs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Tanic, just answer the questions. Mr. Milosevic, let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to hear the name of at least one person that I received at the JUL premises.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He's given his answer. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, at JUL receptions, Mr. Tanic - just give me a yes or no answer - I was a guest there. So then it's not that I received these 1.000 or 1.500 people. I was a guest, like the rest of them were. And since you claim that I received persons at JUL premises, I'm telling you, give me the name of at least one person whom I received at the JUL premises.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Should I give an answer to this question who the people are who had dinners and working meeting with Mr. Milosevic and that can be considered as Mr. Milosevic having received them, although he was a guest there too. I did not even want to refer to the fact that Ms. Markovic is his wife, because I don't want to discuss any personal matters, either my own or Mr. Milosevic's. And of course, under such circumstances --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, how could we have discreet meetings if, as you say, they were held at the MPs' club?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not repeat that part of my statement during my testimony. I have already said that I'm saying during my testimony only those things that can be additionally proven from independent sources.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did I ever receive you at the White Palace, Beli Dvor?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that I never received anyone at the JUL premises or at the club for members of parliament?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We've been over this. There's no point going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that I held all my meetings at the place where I worked? That is to say, at Beli Dvor, the White Palace?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but you were not always the President of Yugoslavia. For a while you were the President of Serbia also, and then you did not use the White Palace, you used the Presidency of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm referring to when I was President of Yugoslavia, and also when I was President of Serbia, again I used my own office.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We've heard evidence about all this. The witness has said what he has. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You claim that during some reception, I singled you out and had a conversation with you. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, may I just say this now? I've seen this page now, the one that Mr. Milosevic referred to. It says the JUL offices here, so it's probably a problem with translation. Here it says the JUL offices or the JUL headquarters rather than the JUL premises. As for the other question, well, yes, yes. Usually you sort of single out the person that you are going to talk to. I'm not trying to say that you run into the cellar or something like that, but you sort of are separated from other people for a longer or shorter period of time, depending on how long you're talking to people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since this was not my custom, can you tell me that I singled one individual out and stood separately with that individual and talked to this individual?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He's answered the question. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was my understanding, on the basis of what you said, that you regularly submitted reports on your work to the leadership of the state security but also to the head of your party, Dusan Mihajlovic. Did I understand that correctly?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You did understand it correctly, provided that the wording implies that they were aware of the results of my work. Sometimes it is a report, sometimes it's not a report. You see, notes can be made in the form of proposals, reports, in five or six different ways, but they were always accurately informed as to what I was doing and what we were doing, and it was always the same kind of information that was provided.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, because I participated in that, Mr. Milosevic. If I informed someone, then I imagine I should know that I informed them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh. Are you saying that you informed me personally, eye-to-eye?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know what? The first meeting that I mentioned to you when the platform was presented to you, of course I informed you eye-to-eye. Of course we were not sitting in the cellar or in the bathroom or whatever. I am referring to the meeting when the platform was presented and when it was discussed. It was not only that that was discussed. Collective security in the Balkans was discussed and other questions. So I'm referring to that first meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh. So you claim that when I received the delegation of Novo Demokratija, that was that; right?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is one of the examples. You see, it can be proven. This is an example I used to illustrate this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, then, show it. Prove it, if you can.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I can prove it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, prove it, if you can prove it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. Get on with the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did I understand this correctly? Because you only partially answered my questions. You reported to the leadership of the state security and also to the head of your party, Dusan Mihajlovic. I understood you correctly on that one; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you did not understand me right. I said that they were informed. Sometimes these were reports. Sometimes this was communication. Sometimes it was a different form of providing information, because "report" seems to imply being an informer and especially as far as the state security is concerned. That's the way it's looked upon in our country.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Forget about that. Did I understand you correctly that you were reporting to the leadership of the state security and to the head of your party, Dusan Mihajlovic?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, in different forms. In different forms. Not always in writing, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. To both. Does that mean that Dusan Mihajlovic was also an associate of the State Security Service?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is that a question or a statement?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no. It's a question. I put it very nicely. Does that mean that Dusan Mihajlovic was an associate of the state security?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not here to testify about Mr. Dusan Mihajlovic or is his status the subject of any kind of debate. Nobody was an associate. Dusan Mihajlovic was president of one of the ruling parties until 1997, until he left the coalition, because you violated the agreement and because of the problems that you started to make.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. Next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. If he was not an associate of the state security, as that is how I understand your answer, why did you submit parallel reports to him as you did to the state security?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You cannot understand from my answer that he was not an associate of the state security. I didn't say yes, I didn't say no. However, I said that anybody in the capacity of one of the heads of one of the leading parties --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The question is: Why did you submit reports parallel to both him and the state security? That is the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because part of the question had to do strictly with the security component and it's the State Security Service that is in charge of that. They were supposed to assess whether that does exist or does not exist as a problem. It's not any politician who should do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If he was not an associate too, why did he have to be aware of the information that you were giving to the State Security Service?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I did not hide that. These were legal political issues and their security component. There is no need for you to hide something that is part of regular work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did people from the state security know that you were providing information simultaneously to someone else as well?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would kindly ask for the question to be rephrased so I can understand it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You want me to put the question to you again; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To rephrase it, because I don't understand it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were people from the State Security Service aware of the fact that you were providing this information at the same time to somebody else as well?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The political part of the information, yes. There is no contest about that, because as for the political issues involved, there are several strata within them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So can I understand this to mean that they did know that you were giving information to someone else as well?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The way you have put it, no, that's not the way I had put it. I was quite specific. They were aware of the political part of this information, that it was being provided to someone else too, because I was, first and foremost, a politician.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And what was it that you were doing that was so important that I should be informed daily as to your work? I wasn't informed -- I didn't inform myself on the work of any institution like that, even MUP, the foreign affairs ministry, the General Staff, and so on, daily. I didn't do that.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is that on a page of my statement or what?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you said this.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that on a daily basis, you had contacts with the State Security Service and quite certainly you were informed frequently about my own work too, because some questions were such that what we did, I was able to recognise in what you were doing, and I received information as well that you had been informed about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who gave you that information?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the leadership of the State Security Service. You know, the people who do this don't hold it in a drawer of their desk, especially when you're talking about Kosovo and other vital questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that means that they informed you that they were supplying me with information that you were supplying them with; is that it?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, this is routine techniques in all countries all over the world as well as in Serbia and Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, just because it is routine technique and because you say that you are acquainted with the rules of service, do you know that you don't inform as to whom you're distributing information to that was amassed concerning a member, for example?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When we're dealing with a large number of individuals. But when they are individuals that have to make decisions on the basis of that and when you recognise in the work of those individuals what you had spent doing ten days previously, then it is obvious. For example, me for confidence building measures, for example.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What confidence building measures?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm taking that as an example to illustrate to this Court. You didn't mention confidence building measures before I -- before this was placed on the table before me and others as a step forward in our negotiations with the Albanians. And then you started mentioning this and applying it. To the great satisfaction of one and all, you concluded this confidence building -- this set of confidence building measures by the agreement on education. And then I put it into practice. But there are no secrets. What you're talking about, the secrets you're talking about refer to espionage and none of us dealt in that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So do you claim that you knew about the education agreement before it was signed and published in the papers on the 1st of September, 1996? Is that it?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. I even took part, in a way, in previous preparations for that. And later on, it came into your hands and Mr. Paglia's hands, Mr. Rugova's hands and Ratko Markovic's hands. Of course I was informed. How would I not be? Because it was on the basis of our recommendations that this confidence building set of measures was devised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'm asking you because, up to the present day, I had believed that this was due to Mr. Paglia as a senior member of the humanitarian community of the Sant' Egidio community and that he was a humanitarian and Christian man and that he did this independently. I didn't know he did that at your initiative. So you say that Paglia did this at your initiative, do you?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't say that Monsignor Paglia did this at my initiative, but together with the Italian Ambassador, Francesco Sconi [phoen], and together with myself and the president of my party, Mr. Dusan Mihajlovic, and even together with Vuk Draskovic, he took part in some negotiations, two or three talks with Dojcilo Maslovaric as well, where there was an exchange of views as to what could be done to build confidence and how to start boosting confidence. And he had a similar initiative. You never have the initiative of one man in politics. What I said about myself I said about myself because I am here to testify, but otherwise this implies that there is always an exchange of views in politics, and I saw Mr. Paglia on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just be brief, please; shorter answers, please. Does that mean that you claim you took part in the work of -- Don Vincenzo Paglia's work before the agreement appeared in public on education that was signed by myself and Rugova?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely so. And Don Vincenzo Paglia, in the meantime, became a Bishop and we saw each other quite recently, relatively speaking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All I wanted to do was to ascertain that. So you say that before we signed the education agreement, you yourself were included, involved, together with Don Vincenzo Paglia, in the activities to prepare the agreement on education, to pave the way for the education agreement.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And with some other people of goodwill. Some of them were your associates, some of them were foreign diplomats; this is no secret.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But he claimed it was, you see. So I hope that we'll be able to clear that matter up too. And do you know where that agreement was written, was compiled? If you know everything about it, do you know where it was written?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Don Vincenzo Paglia kept the agreement as a secret, not the preparations of the agreement, so let's not confuse the two. Later on, when the agreement was prepared in principle, they went on to prepare it in more concrete terms. Mr. Ratko Markovic went to Rome in the formal and legal sense, who had firmer authorisation. I think that Mr. Maslovaric took part in the agreement, and then the agreement was taken to Mr. Rugova to be signed in Pristina, and then it was brought to you for you to sign. So after Rugova signed it, you did. The only thing you did was to avoid the fact that Monsignor Paglia should appear at some joint reception to do away with this side altogether. So to all practical intents and purposes, Mr. Paglia took the agreement to Mr. Rugova, Rugova signed it, it was brought to you, you signed it, and then Mr. Paglia didn't appear there any more. So he kept it in secret, he kept it confidential, not because nobody else took part but to save face for official Belgrade and for Rugova and you to be the main actors, and you were the main two, the principal two people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please. Are you conscious of the fact that he could not appear simultaneously in Pristina and Belgrade as the agreement was signed -- Rugova signed it in Pristina and I signed it later on that same day in Belgrade? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wasn't saying where Mr. Monsignor Paglia was. Quite obviously from your question, I know that it was signed first in Pristina and then in Belgrade, and we have both confirmed that I know the details with respect to the technique in which the document was signed, although I needn't have known because I took part in its preparation and not in its signing and writing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said a moment ago that the intention for him not to appear was that his participation should be avoided so that the public should not be made aware of his participation in the matter, that it should remain between us, the two main people, Rugova and myself, without seeing his participation in it all publicly. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We must be very precise there. It was your wish not to have the third party's participation obvious, because this was the third side, third element. But in preparation for the agreement here and there, you would allow this, and this was the case with other agreements too. You allowed Monsignor Paglia to appear here and there and to pave the way in public for it to go ahead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. As you're acquainted with the agreement that Rugova and myself signed, may I remind you that it says in the agreement that the two of us extend our gratitude to our mutual friends from the humanitarian community of Sant' Egidio for their contribution to bringing about the agreement. Are you aware of that? Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I know about that, of course. But you didn't want him to be physically present. You extended your gratitude to Holbrooke and Ivor Robertson and so on. You were friends with them and had quarrels with them but you never wanted anybody, any third party to be physically present, otherwise your history of good and bad relations with many people is common knowledge and common public knowledge, and that is nothing strange.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tanic, please, I am here to cross-examine you with respect to your statement. You said -- and testimony. You said a moment ago that he was not present because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We've exhausted this topic. Let's move on to something else.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's easy to check that out anyway, because he's an honest man. Now, why -- why do you consider, or did you consider, or do you consider that Serbia and the Serbian people would share your opinion about the fact that the Albanians should be given the role of being the Piedmont of southern Europe?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that I had that kind of opinion. Perhaps I might have let slip something like that here or there. But otherwise, my opinion as to the contents of the agreement stemmed from what was decided upon within the ruling coalition; formally, informally, at whatever level you like.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me read out on page 5, the end of the third paragraph from the bottom, page 5 of your statement, in which you claim that in this approach for autonomy, the model of the South Tyrol was used. My thinking behind this proposal, and which informed my negotiation with the Kosovo Albanians, was to give them what they wanted most, which was to be the Piedmont of southern Europe, so that they would forget about rebellion. The objective was to come up with a framework for agreement on a solution to the crisis in Kosovo that the Serbian government would sign later. Et cetera. Next paragraph. So you say: "My thinking behind this proposal was that they should be allowed to be the Piedmont of southern Europe." So that that is what should be given them in order to avoid their bestiality.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, quite obviously there's a typing error. And nobody can be the Piedmont of southern Europe. There can only be a Piedmont in southern Europe. And it was my thinking that we should give them what they wanted to have them refrain and forget about rebellion. I think that is quite proper, quite proper thinking. And if I said or used the term the Piedmont of southern Europe, I never defended that publicly, and the statement given in English, one can describe something sometimes but it is quite clearly stated they should be given something to forget about their rebellion and I think that was quite a proper stand which was supported by the Serbs as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, as you keep using the term "colloquial," what do you think "colloquial" means?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, "colloquial" means something when somebody uses ordinary everyday speech to describe a phenomenon or concept which in its working version is described more precisely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, as you say you're well-versed in the Kosovo Albanian circumstances, how do you claim that their rebellion could be so destructive that their alternative would be their Piedmont position in southern Europe, no more no less, but you have the Greeks there, the Bulgarians, the Romanians, and all the others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Time has now run out, in fact, this being a lengthy question. Mr. Milosevic, this cross-examination will continue on Tuesday of next week, but your time will be limited, and you should prepare on the basis that you will have another hour and a half. So during that time, any questions you want to ask, you must ask. Mr. Tanic, would you be back, please, at 9.00 on Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before we adjourn, can we take a look at the book named Fire and Flood? Who is keeping this book? Mr. Milosevic, do you have the book with you now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I haven't got it with me.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. The microphone is off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Microphone. Well, in any event, we'll have that book. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I was simply saying I think it was provided to the accused yesterday, and it looks as though he may have inadvertently taken it with him and --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I received it yesterday, but I can't carry all these papers about in my bag. I didn't know that I had to give it back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let us have it back sometime.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.
